questions.title: What Is One Major Benefit Of Using An LLM Only During Training Rather Than For Every Prediction?
questions.question_body:
I learned that FEAT​LLVM feeds GPT once during training stages then drops it afterward.
Does keeping GPT "offline" truly reduce inference latency compared
with directly requesting predictions through its API?
Can you clarify how eliminating per‑sample calls translates into lower computational cost?

questions.title: Why Does FEAT​LLVM Restrict Rule Generation To Ten Rules Per Class?
questions.question_body:
The paper mentions cutting off extraction at ten rules.
Is this limit tied mainly to token budget constraints,
or do fewer/more rules lead respectively to underfitting or massive prompt growth?
Has changing that hyperparameter been shown experimentally?

questions.title: How Are Categorical Columns Handled When Rules Are Generated By GPT?
questions.question_body:
Rules sometimes involve comparisons such as ‘feature V equals healthy’. If a category label isn’t listed among a column’s possible options,
how does FEAT​LLVM make sure attributes have compatible types before turning them into executable conditionals?
Are synonym mappings designed automatically?

questions.title: Converting Noisy Natural Language Rules Into Executable Code
questions.question_body:
Describe how FEAT​LLVM turns its somewhat informal model outputs into runnable Python snippets.
After receiving diverse wording from GPT,
how does it reliably build a small program that evaluates each row against every generated condition?

questions.title: Why Must Weight Vectors Be Projected Onto Their Positive Part Before Dotting With Binary Features?
questions.question_body:
FEAT​LLVM forces non‑negative weights through "max(· , 0)".
Besides keeping probabilities non‑negative,
how does this operation affect learning dynamics?
Is it related simply to monotonicity between satisfying a rule and increasing target probability?

questions.title: Effect Of Bagging Size On Accuracy
questions.question_body:
Bagging provides randomness over subsets of samples or features.
Do larger bags always improve performance,
or do diminishing returns appear around certain sizes?
What trade‑off did experiments observe between bag size, ensemble size, and run time?

questions.title: Role Of Two-Step Reasoning Instruction In Avoiding Spurious Correlations
questions.question_body:
FEAT​LLVM splits reasoning into:
a prior inference based on background knowledge;
a empirical confirmation based on few-shot demos.
How does isolating intent help prevent picking up noise columns
and enforce selection of variables truly related to the target?

questions.title: Computing AUROC For Each Rule Feature Prior To Linear Weight Training
questions.question_body:
Before fitting weights,
the paper reports an AUROC score per binary-rule column.
Explain how true positives / false positives / negatives are counted
for one rule across training examples
and why AUROC > 0½ signals useful information.

questions.title: Why Can Unseen Domains Still Obtain High Accuracy With FEAT​LLVM?
Extending FEAT​LLVM To Regression Tasks
questions.question_body:
FEAT​LLVM currently assumes categorical labels.
If one wants continuous targets,
do we replace softmax + cross entropy
with alternative loss networks
and adapt linear weighting scheme differently?
What practical changes would be required?
